subject: Throughput gating & streaming handshake — post-demo next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acrohealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acrohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Throughput gating & streaming handshake — post-demo next steps

Thanks again for joining the demo this morning — appreciate the focused run-through of your streaming use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we scope the PoC.

Key notes from the session:
- Target tail latency: 95th percentile <= 220ms for 512-token responses (average prompt length ~40 tokens).
- Sustained throughput target: 180 requests/minute for the initial integration (burst to 400 rpm during peak windows).
- Concurrency: expected 40 concurrent sessions from web app layer; each session issues 1–2 parallel generation calls.
- Streaming: client requires chunked streaming with partial tokens every 120ms to support progressive rendering.
- Gotchas: encrypted payload size and KV-cache warmup on cold starts were observed in the demo — may affect first-token latency by ~50–120ms.

Attachments: I uploaded the demo recording and a first-pass SLO gating checklist (attached).

Proposed MAP (short):
1) Redwood provides a focused PoC configuration: 4x A100-equivalent serving nodes, 2x quantized model variant, streaming hooks & prefix cache enabled.
2) AcroHealth runs a 3-day load window with synthetic load shaped to 180 rpm steady / 400 rpm burst.
3) We collect token-level traces and a short prompt set (you to share 8–10 common prompts).
4) Decision criteria: pass if 95p latency <= 220ms for >= 90% of run and streaming frames delivered within 200ms of generation.

Can you confirm the prompt set and the dates you prefer for the PoC window? If that looks good, we’ll schedule a short kickoff with infra and SRE (Ben + Marissa).

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Dylan — the recap is helpful. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates:

1) For 95p <= 220ms, is that measured end-to-end (client observed) or server-side only (after ingress)? We need client-observed numbers to own the UX requirement.
2) Streaming frame cadence: 120ms was an ask from Product; can we tolerate up to 200ms for first frames during cold starts?
3) Concurrency: 40 sessions is our expected steady-state. During marketing spikes we could see short bursts to 120 concurrent sessions.

We can share the 10 prompts by EOD Monday. Target PoC window: Aug 24–26 (3 days) — does that work for Redwood?

Also — we have an internal security checklist; Ben/Marissa, you’ll probably want the SOC2 scoping info (I can provide the contact).

Best,
Samira

Quick technical points from our SRE side:
- Measurement: we’ll instrument both server-side (ingress->egress) and client-observed using a lightweight beacon you can embed. For the PoC acceptance, we recommend client-observed as the final gating metric (agree with Samira).
- Cold starts: enabling prefix/KV cache persistence across warm pools reduces first-token variance; we saw ~40–80ms improvement in our internal runs. Full cold (empty cache) can add 100–150ms. We’ll include a cache-warmup step in the PoC script.
- Streaming cadence: server can push partial frames every ~100–140ms depending on token generation variance. Network jitter on client side can add another 20–80ms. For acceptance, we can set a soft requirement: 90% of streaming chunks within 220ms, with an allowance for the first chunk during hard cold starts up to 320ms.

I’ve attached the kv-cache-profile.txt with the timeline we observed in the demo.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv-cache-profile.txt

Subject: Re: Throughput gating & streaming handshake — post-demo next steps

Thanks Samira — Aug 24–26 works from our side. Summary of updated acceptance criteria based on Ben/Samira notes:
- Final gating metric: client-observed 95th percentile latency <= 220ms for 512-token responses over the 3-day run.
- Streaming frames: 90% of frames delivered within 220ms; allowance for first-frame cold starts up to 320ms.
- Throughput: steady-state 180 rpm; system must not exceed error rate of 1.5% during sustained load.
- Concurrency tolerance: support 40 steady concurrent sessions and handle short spikes up to 120 concurrent sessions for at least 10 minutes without degradation below SLO.

Prep items for AcroHealth (Raj/Samira):
- Share 8–12 canonical prompts and expected average response lengths.
- Provide a staging endpoint where the client beacon can be accepted (sample script included in the Drive link).
- Confirm any IP allowlist or egress constraints for the PoC.

Redwood deliverables before kickoff:
- PoC runbook + load script (we’ll post this link by Aug 20).
- Instrumentation guidance for client-observed telemetry.
- Access to a temporary SRE point-of-contact for 24–48h of the run (Ben will be on-call).

Next step: I’ll send a calendar invite for an Aug 23 kickoff (30m) to sync on load scripts and telemetry. Can you confirm attendees for that call?

-Dylan
